answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit work, and a random sample of its outputs is checked against later, independently verified results. A failed check burns the stake and blocks the agent from future rounds. Spinning up a thousand identities therefore requires a thousand funded locks, not just new accounts; the attacker risks losing real capital per identity. A jetty, an island, and a zephyr may sound like distinct agents, but none can cheaply multiply that stake.
